solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brittle fellow who is mad accommodated by society's extremists

indicators.note: being accommodated by someone means being housed within their home, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: the first and last letters of 'society'
the proverbial madman, from 'mad as a hatter'

explanation.surface: A fragile, unstable man is taken in by the fringe members of polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: The hatter sits inside S...Y, giving SHATTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattery is a dialect or Chambers word for something easily broken, fragile like glass.

clue.text: Scottish dish the reverse of fresh features in call for help

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word written from its end back to its start
to feature in something is to appear within it, so one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: A Scottish recipe is said to put fresh ingredients into an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: SOS is the Morse distress call; 'the reverse of' applies only to the word for fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowens is a traditional Scots porridge made from fermented oat husks and meal.

clue.text: Euro-partisan turned out to be like an old reptile

indicators.note: something turned out has been tipped over and reshaped, so its letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: all twelve letters, the hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A fervent Europhile is mocked as a dinosaur, an old fossil out of touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jibe 'old reptile' for an old-fashioned politician hides the literal flying reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterosaurian is the adjective for the pterosaurs, the extinct flying reptiles of the dinosaur age.

clue.text: Young animal in distress overlooked by good person

indicators.note: in a down entry, being overlooked by something means sitting below it, so that piece comes second

blocks.note: to irk is to annoy or distress

explanation.surface: A young creature in trouble is watched over by a kindly soul.
explanation.walkthrough: ST for a saint, a 'good person', is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirk is a yearling bullock or heifer, a young cow between one and two years old.

clue.text: After a cold, girl gets spicy cake

indicators.note: the girl comes after the illness, fixing the order of the two pieces

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a cold treats herself to a hot spiced bake.
explanation.definitionFit: A chillada is a Mexican cake or fritter of vegetables and chilli, so spicy is the key.

clue.text: The fellow's taking leading position for a month

blocks.note: the van is the front of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A man takes the lead for a whole month.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesvan, or Heshvan, is the second month of the Jewish civil year, falling in October or November.

clue.text: Japan's not first to get winning scores in judo

indicators.note: not first tells you to drop the opening letter

blocks.note: Nippon is the Japanese name for Japan, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: Japan, not coming first, still wins points in its national martial art.
explanation.definitionFit: An ippon is a full point in judo, ending the contest outright in the scorer's favour.

clue.text: Origin of language said to be in part of the head

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Where speech comes from is said to lie somewhere in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' here is a plain synonym for spoken, not a sound-alike signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Loral describes the lore, the region between eye and bill or snout in birds and reptiles.

clue.text: Took note, being excited about minister and duke turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: Someone took notice, stirred up as a clergyman and nobleman appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turning up' reverses the minister-and-duke pair, which then splits the word for excited in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is to turn the mind to something, to remark on or criticise it.

clue.text: Modern technology embraced by European Mormon

indicators.note: being embraced is being held within someone's arms, so one piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A European church member takes up new gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danites were a secret band of early Latter-day Saints, so a Danite is a member of that Mormon group.

clue.text: Attractive person is too much in hurry

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: A good-looking person is said to be overdoing the rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A hottie is slang for a sexually attractive person.

clue.text: Eggs, any number in store mostly used for making sort of cake

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
in places the eggs and number inside the other word

blocks.note: to pack away is to store
N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Eggs in quantity from the larder go into baking a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: O stands for an egg by its shape; the eggs and number go inside the shortened word for store.
explanation.definitionFit: Poonac is coconut oil-cake, the residue pressed from coconut kernels and used as cattle feed.

clue.text: A German gentleman with inner power in a team is amazing

indicators.note: having something inner means it is placed inside
in puts the German article and gentleman inside the team

blocks.note: a wing is a group or faction, a team

explanation.surface: A German man who brings real strength to a side is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German' is the German word for a, not an abbreviation; a wing is a team in the sense of a squad or faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awe-inspiring fills you with wonder, which is what amazing means.

clue.text: Boy to go wrong stuffing empty plaything with fabric

indicators.note: an empty thing has had its contents removed, leaving only its outside letters
stuffing means filling, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A naughty lad fills a hollowed-out toy with cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is defined twice, once at each end, with the wordplay between.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry is a boy's name, and terry is also the looped cotton cloth used for towels.

clue.text: Japanese lord king gives the boot

blocks.note: kami is a Japanese title for a lord or noble

explanation.surface: A Japanese nobleman and a king dismiss someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives the boot' reads as sacking someone; here the boot is literal footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A kamik is an Inuit sealskin boot.

clue.text: This letter is read out in a coffee-house

indicators.note: reading something out means voicing it, so the answer matches the sound

blocks.note: a caff is a British slang word for a cheap cafe

explanation.surface: A letter is read aloud to the customers in a cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaph is the eleventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: What's all right about article presenting a riddle?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Asking whether an essay posing a puzzle is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A koan is a Zen Buddhist paradox or riddle used to provoke enlightenment.

clue.text: What's Celt worn when dancing? Small head ornament

indicators.note: dancing sends things whirling about, so the letters move into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Asking what a Celtic dancer wears on stage, perhaps a little circlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A crownlet is a little crown, an ornament worn on the head.

clue.text: Terrible noises brought by excuse in court

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A dreadful racket is used as a defendant's excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An essoin is an old legal term for an excuse for not appearing in court when summoned.

clue.text: Palm trees burning from the ground up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going from the ground up means reading from the bottom

blocks.note: sati or suttee is the historic Hindu practice of a widow's self-burning

explanation.surface: Palms are on fire from the roots upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The ita is the miriti palm of South America, so itas are palm trees.

clue.text: One digging in spring with skin getting a bit flaked off

indicators.note: a bit flaking off means one small piece is lost from the end

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring
derm is a variant of derma, skin

explanation.surface: A gardener digging in springtime finds the skin peeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a mineral spring; DERM loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spader is someone who digs with a spade, or a digging machine.

clue.text: Old money they shelled out for US property

indicators.note: shelling something removes its inner content, so only the outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: People paid old-fashioned cash for a piece of American real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled out' reads as paid, but here it means the middle of a word is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is the American term for real estate, land and buildings as property.

clue.text: Stab that could make me leap around

indicators.note: moving letters around means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A sudden stab would make anyone jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Empale is a variant spelling of impale, to pierce with a pointed stake.

clue.text: Most ready to have a break after end of journey

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
after places the rest following the letter taken from the journey

explanation.surface: Someone most prepared for a stop once the trip is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Yare is an old word for nimble or ready, so the superlative yarest means readiest.

clue.text: Quiet one, very old with love for noisy party?

explanation.surface: One quiet, elderly person in love is hardly suited to a rowdy gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivoo is Australian slang for a boisterous party or celebration.

clue.text: Military commander given title of respect — bold, not half!

indicators.note: not half means half the word is thrown away

explanation.surface: A general is knighted for half-hearted courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sirdar is a commander or chief in India and the Middle East, notably the British commander of the Egyptian army.

clue.text: Hoteliers may have replaced the windows here

indicators.note: things replaced are put back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Hotel owners might have had new windows fitted in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus THE rearranges to HOTELIERS, so take THE out of the jumble to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriels are bay windows that project from an upper storey.

clue.text: What's endlessly painful? Don't mention it!

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter

blocks.note: bitter means painful, as in a bitter blow

explanation.surface: Asking what hurts, only to be told not to bring it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is German, the stock reply to thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitte is German for you're welcome, the polite reply meaning no thanks are needed.

clue.text: Language isn't common mostly, acceptable to the well-bred?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

blocks.note: ain't is the vulgar, common form of isn't

explanation.surface: Asking whether vulgar speech is mostly fine among the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ainu is the language of the indigenous people of northern Japan.

clue.text: Fast runner in bar fixing things

explanation.surface: A sprinter in a pub sorts things out.
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is Usain Bolt, written with his initial; 'bar' is not a pub but a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-bolt is a U-shaped metal rod threaded at both ends, used as a clamp or fastener.

clue.text: Besotted characters in the prison

indicators.note: characters in means the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Infatuated inmates of a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Epris is French-derived for enamoured or smitten, in love.

clue.text: Poison poisoner finally dumped in a rubbish container

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter
dumped in means thrown inside

explanation.surface: The poison of a murderer ends up thrown in the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrin is a highly toxic protein found in the seeds of the rosary pea.

clue.text: Steward tolerated him when drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A waiter put up with a guest who had had too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A maître d'hôtel is the head waiter or house steward in a restaurant or grand household.

clue.text: Wind in plain to the west side of America

indicators.note: in an across entry the west is the left, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: a flat is a level plain

explanation.surface: A breeze over the Great Plains in the western United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The weather picture of wind on the prairie hides the bodily kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatus is gas in the gut or expelled from it, wind in the digestive sense.

clue.text: Gene Kelly edges away, rolling over in drink

indicators.note: with the edges gone, only the middle letters remain
rolling over flips something end to end
in places it inside the drink

explanation.surface: Gene Kelly sidles away and falls over drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gene Kelly' reads as the dancer, but Gene is the definition and Kelly the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An allele is one of the alternative forms of a gene at a given locus.

clue.text: A Romeo comes back to home — female deprived of male first seen here?

definitions.text: A Romeo comes back to home — female deprived of male first seen here?

indicators.note: being deprived of something means losing it, so those letters are removed
coming back means running in the opposite direction
first puts this piece at the front of the answer

blocks.note: taken as written, then removed from the previous word
R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo returns to the house, and where is the woman first spotted? At the window, as Juliet was.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: Juliet is first seen by Romeo at her window, which is the Latin word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestra is Latin for window, used in anatomy for a window-like opening.
